title: M-52
excerpt: A sulfate-process rutile titanium dioxide pigment documented for printing inks, can coatings and high-gloss interior architectural coatings.

data.h1: M-52 Titanium Dioxide for Printing Inks and Coatings Evaluation
hero_paragraphs: The current M-52 product profile identifies very high gloss, high opacity, excellent dispersion and low abrasivity as evaluation directions for printing ink and selected coating applications. Review the typical product data below and confirm suitability through testing in your own formulation, dispersion process, application and end-use conditions.

data.positioning_title: Where M-52 Fits in Product Evaluation
positioning_paragraphs: M-52 is a rutile titanium dioxide pigment produced by the sulfate process and documented for the printing ink industry and selected coating applications.

Use M-52 as an evaluation candidate when gloss, opacity, dispersion and abrasivity are relevant to the project. Final Grade selection should account for the complete formulation, binder or vehicle, dispersion process, pigment loading, substrate, application method, curing conditions, service environment and destination-document needs.
facts: Evaluation of gloss, opacity, dispersion and abrasivity
data.applications_title: Printing Ink and Coating Directions to Evaluate

applications.title: Printing Inks
applications.text: Evaluate M-52 in the intended printing-ink vehicle and dispersion process. Confirm gloss, opacity, dispersion, abrasivity, color and print-film performance with the actual formulation and application method.

applications.title: Can Coatings
applications.text: Review M-52 in can-coating formulation testing using the intended binder, substrate, application and curing conditions. Confirm gloss, opacity, dispersion, film appearance and required end-use performance.

applications.title: High-Gloss Interior Architectural Coatings
applications.text: Include M-52 in high-gloss interior architectural coating evaluation. Confirm optical targets, dispersion, finished-film appearance, formulation compatibility and service performance under the intended interior conditions.

data.evaluation_title: What to Evaluate in Your Formulation

evaluation.title: Optical and Film Review
items: Gloss target in the complete ink or coating formulation
Opacity at the intended pigment loading and film thickness
Dispersion behavior in the selected vehicle, binder and process
Color and finished-film appearance under the actual application conditions

evaluation.title: Processing and Qualification Review
items: Abrasivity direction in the intended dispersion, printing or application equipment
Compatibility with the full formulation and additive package
Printing-ink, can-coating or interior architectural conditions, as applicable
Substrate, application method, curing, destination requirements and sample-validation results
